region: Europe (France, Belgium, Germany, Greece, Italy, Portugal, Spain)
key_facts: As retirees live longer, governments need to spend more on pensions, making it harder to fund other services; this has spurred protests, including planned nationwide antigovernment demonstrations in France on Saturday.
Recent protests driven by young people have taken place in Belgium, Germany, Greece, Italy and Portugal.
Pensions are routinely the largest items in Europe's national budgets, and the article frames the issue as a 'generational clash' between young people's needs and retirees' pension payments.

Sébastien Ducros, a 36-year-old French data analyst, argues that a large share of state money goes to retirees while schools and other services are neglected; Laurent Grinwald, a 72-year-old recently retired postal worker, opposes any pension reduction, citing rising rents and cost of living.
importance_reason: Broad European fiscal and social-policy trend with planned mass protests in France, but a feature-style piece without new official data or policy decisions.
market_link: Pension spending pressure on national budgets could affect sovereign bond issuance and fiscal outlooks, but the article gives no specific market-relevant figures or decisions.

key_facts: The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all flights shortly before 4 p.m. Eastern on Friday; per Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, more than 3,500 planes were in the air at the time.

Duffy attributed the ground stop to aging radar and communications equipment that became overloaded; the stop was lifted just over four hours after it was announced, the longest nationwide air ban since Sept. 11, 2001.
Over 6,600 flights were canceled by 9:30 p.m. Eastern on Friday, and 1,500 flights scheduled for Saturday were also canceled; the source says delays will likely last for days.
importance_reason: Major national disruption to air travel with significant cancellation volumes, but no direct market-moving data or policy decision in the text.
market_link: Airline stocks and aviation-related equities could react to the cancellations and any associated costs; effect is uncertain from the source alone.
